blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Many IT projects fail. But the problem is not always the technology. Often, nobody explained the project clearly to the people who pay for it.

A non-technical stakeholder wants to know three things: Is the project on track? What is the next milestone? What could go wrong? The answer should be short, honest, and in normal business language. No jargon.

If you must use a technical term, explain it in one sentence. For example: "We are testing integration with the bank system. This means we check that both systems exchange the right information without errors. We expect to finish by Friday." Stakeholders do not need to be experts. They need to trust that the team makes honest, thoughtful decisions. Clear communication builds that trust.

items.q: According to the text, why do many IT projects fail?
options: Nobody explained the project clearly to the people who pay
items.why: "the problem is not always the technology... nobody explained the project clearly to the people who pay for it."

items.q: What three things does a non-technical stakeholder want to know?
options: The budget, the team, and the office
Is it on track, what is the next milestone, what could go wrong
The code, the servers, and the tests
The past, the present, and the future
items.why: "is the project on track, what is the next milestone, and what could go wrong."

items.q: What should you do if you must use a technical term?
options: Send a long list to the stakeholder
Ask the stakeholder to study it
items.why: "If you must use a technical word, explain it in one sentence."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Stakeholders should trust the team's decisions
Stakeholders must learn all the technical words to understand a project
Reports should use normal business language
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz "Stakeholders do not need to become experts" — eles não precisam aprender o jargão.

items.q: The example about the bank system suggests that…
options: a hard word becomes clear with one simple sentence
the team will miss the deadline
items.why: Inferência: o exemplo mostra como explicar "integration" em uma frase simples e clara.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie reescrever um relatório de projeto de TI para um executivo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, let me look at this project update together with you. It has five technical terms, and I think that is the real problem here. You are not an engineer, so you should not need to be one to read this.

Look at this line: "We are running an API integration." That means nothing to you. So let me change it. I will write: "We are connecting our system to the bank's system, so they can share information automatically." Now you understand it, right?

Here is the next one. The report says "latency is high." I will write instead: "The system is a bit slow, so we are fixing it this week." Simple.

I do this for all five terms. One short sentence each. No jargon. And look at your face now — you finally understand the project. That is the whole point. You do not need to be an expert. You just need to trust that we are making honest, thoughtful decisions. That trust starts with clear words.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie think is the real problem with the update?
items.why: "It has five technical terms, and I think that is the real problem here."

items.q: How does Sophie explain "API integration"?
options: She says the systems connect and share information automatically
She adds three more technical words
She asks the executive to study it
items.why: "We are connecting our system to the bank's system, so they can share information automatically."

items.q: Instead of "latency is high," what does Sophie write?
options: The system is a bit slow, so we are fixing it this week
items.why: "The system is a bit slow, so we are fixing it this week."

items.q: Why does Sophie say "look at your face now"?
options: The executive finally understands the project
items.why: Inferência: as palavras simples fizeram o executivo entender pela primeira vez.

items.q: What does Sophie believe the executive really needs?
options: To trust that the team makes honest, thoughtful decisions
items.why: Inferência: "You do not need to be an expert. You just need to trust that we are making honest, thoughtful decisions."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Every stakeholder will get the report on Friday." A stakeholder is…
options: a person with an interest in the project
items.why: Stakeholder = parte interessada: quem tem interesse no projeto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Good news — the project is ___ and we will finish on time."
items.why: On track = no caminho: seguindo bem o plano.

items.q: "We reached an important milestone today." A milestone is…
options: a key point or step in the project
items.why: Milestone = marco: um ponto importante do projeto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please write the report without ___ so everyone can understand it."
items.why: Jargon = jargão: palavras técnicas que confundem quem não é da área.

items.q: "The two systems exchange information every hour." To exchange means to…
items.why: To exchange = trocar: um dá e o outro recebe.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de projetos de TI. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the report." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Next month we will roll out the new system to all teams." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = lançar, colocar em uso.

items.q: "Some stakeholders pushed back on the new deadline." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "We must keep the stakeholders in the loop about the risks." This means we should…
options: keep them out of the project
items.why: Keep in the loop = manter informado, atualizado.

items.q: "Let's touch base every Friday to check the project." To touch base means to…
items.why: Touch base = fazer um contato rápido para se atualizar.
